title: AI Developer Claims Open-Source Adobe Clones, Declares 'Software Is Over'
title_zh: AI开发者推出开源Adobe克隆软件，宣称“软件时代已终结”
lead: A developer has unveiled a suite of open-source apps that mimic Adobe's Creative Cloud, built with AI assistance and promising full feature parity within months. The ambitious project raises both excitement and legal questions.

paragraphs: For those weary of Adobe's costly and cumbersome Creative Suite, free alternatives have long existed, replicating some or all of its capabilities. Now, developer Brandon Thomas is employing AI-powered reverse engineering to mimic the look, feel, and functionality of Adobe's flagship software with what he hopes will soon be perfect fidelity. His brand, Artcraft, initially a controllable AI for artists, pivoted over the weekend to a suite of seven open-source apps recreating interfaces and tools from Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro.

Announcing the apps on Reddit, Thomas revealed he used Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 to create 'clean-room replacements' in Rust, with WebAssembly versions for browsers. While commenters on Hacker News and elsewhere have pointed out numerous shortcomings, Thomas boldly promises that the current 'super early alpha' will soon match Adobe's functionality. 'We're going to reach 100% [feature] parity within a month,' he stated on Reddit, later amending on Hacker News that '99% parity will take a while, but I'm sure it'll be measured in months and not years.'

Thomas, who claims a decade of experience with large-scale Rust projects, was inspired to build these alternatives after being 'bit by the dark pattern cancellation fee one too many times.' The totally free options, under MIT/Apache licenses, will be funded by selling token-based access to the pre-existing Artcraft visual AI model and IDE, ensuring the project isn't 'some orphaned small-team project,' he wrote. 'We have a team building popular software for filmmakers, so supporting this is fully funded.'

Thomas is the latest in a long line of coders using AI to accelerate reverse engineering, a practice generally deemed legally acceptable. However, the ArtCraft apps could face legal trouble if their 'trade dress' too closely mimics Adobe's familiar appearance. After coding exclusively with AI tools since February, Thomas envisions a near future when developers can recreate open-source versions of popular paid software to 'take back the internet and own tech forever.' 'Now you can just create 1:1 functional equivalents, clean room, that are highly performant and cross-platform. Nothing is stopping you,' he wrote. 'We'll replace Google Search, we'll build our own smartphones, we'll build better infra. We'll remove all the ads and de-enshittify the entire tech world.' 'Software is over,' he gloated, claiming to have 'one-shotted Photoshop. The whole thing.'
paragraphs_zh: 对于那些厌倦了Adobe昂贵且繁琐的Creative Suite的人来说，免费替代品早已存在，它们复制了部分或全部功能。如今，开发者布兰登·托马斯正利用AI驱动的逆向工程，模仿Adobe旗舰软件的外观、感觉和功能，他希望很快能达到完美的保真度。他的品牌Artcraft最初是一款面向艺术家的可控AI，上周末转向了一套包含七个开源应用的套件，重现了Photoshop、Illustrator、Premiere、Lightroom、After Effects、InDesign和Acrobat Pro的界面和工具。

在Reddit上宣布这些应用时，托马斯透露他使用Anthropic的Claude Opus 5.5以Rust语言创建了“净室替代品”，并提供用于浏览器的WebAssembly版本。尽管Hacker News及其他地方的评论者指出了诸多缺陷，托马斯仍大胆承诺，当前的“超早期alpha”很快将匹配Adobe的功能。他在Reddit上表示：“我们将在一个月内达到100%的功能对等，”随后在Hacker News上修正说：“99%的对等需要一段时间，但我确信会以月而非年来衡量。”
托马斯声称拥有十年大规模Rust项目经验，他因“被暗黑模式的取消费用坑了太多次”而受到启发，开始构建这些替代品。这些完全免费的选项采用MIT/Apache许可证，将通过销售现有Artcraft视觉AI模型和IDE的基于代币的访问来资助，以确保项目不会成为“某个被遗弃的小团队项目”，他写道。“我们有一个为电影制作人构建流行软件的团队，所以支持这个项目资金充足。”

托马斯是众多利用AI加速逆向工程的程序员中的最新一位，这种做法通常被认为在法律上可以接受。然而，如果ArtCraft应用的外观“商业外观”过于模仿Adobe的熟悉外观，仍可能面临法律麻烦。自2月以来完全使用AI工具编码后，托马斯设想在不久的将来，开发者可以重建流行付费软件的开源版本，以“夺回互联网，永远拥有科技”。“现在你可以直接创建1:1的功能等价物，净室，高性能且跨平台。没有什么能阻止你，”他写道。“我们将取代谷歌搜索，我们将建造自己的智能手机，我们将建造更好的基础设施。我们将移除所有广告，让整个科技世界去屎化。”“软件已死，”他得意地宣称，并声称“一枪搞定Photoshop。整个玩意儿。”

His brand, Artcraft, initially a controllable AI for artists, pivoted over the weekend to a suite of seven open-source apps recreating interfaces and tools from Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro.

Announcing the apps on Reddit, Thomas revealed he used Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 to create 'clean-room replacements' in Rust, with WebAssembly versions for browsers. While commenters on Hacker News and elsewhere have pointed out numerous shortcomings, Thomas boldly promises that the current 'super early alpha' will soon match Adobe's functionality. 'We're going to reach 100% [feature] parity within a month,' he stated on Reddit, later amending on Hacker News that '99% parity will take a while, but I'm sure it'll be measured in months and not years.'

Thomas, who claims a decade of experience with large-scale Rust projects, was inspired to build these alternatives after being 'bit by the dark pattern cancellation fee one too many times.' The totally free options, under MIT/Apache licenses, will be funded by selling token-based access to the pre-existing Artcraft visual AI model and IDE, ensuring the project isn't 'some orphaned small-team project,' he wrote. 'We have a team building popular software for filmmakers, so supporting this is fully funded.'

Thomas is the latest in a long line of coders using AI to accelerate reverse engineering, a practice generally deemed legally acceptable. However, the ArtCraft apps could face legal trouble if their 'trade dress' too closely mimics Adobe's familiar appearance. After coding exclusively with AI tools since February, Thomas envisions a near future when developers can recreate open-source versions of popular paid software to 'take back the internet and own tech forever.' 'Now you can just create 1:1 functional equivalents, clean room, that are highly performant and cross-platform. Nothing is stopping you,' he wrote. 'We'll replace Google Search, we'll build our own smartphones, we'll build better infra. We'll remove all the ads and de-enshittify the entire tech world.' 'Software is over,' he gloated, claiming to have 'one-shotted Photoshop. The whole thing.'

For a while, those hoping to
avoid the difficulty and expense of dealing with Adobe’s Creative Suite
have been able to use
several free and/or open-source alternatives
that replicate some or all of those capabilities. Now, one developer is using AI-powered reverse engineering to mimic the look, feel, and functionality of Adobe’s well-known software with what he hopes will soon be perfect fidelity.
Artcraft
got its start
last year
as a “controllable AI for artists” that allows for precise post-generation editing of AI-crafted images and videos. Over the weekend, though, the brand
debuted its pivot
to
a suite of seven open source apps
recreating the user interface and tools found in Adobe’s Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro.
In
announcing those new apps on Reddit
earlier this week,
software developer Brandon Thomas
said he used Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 to create “clean-room replacements” for Adobe’s closed source software in Rust (with WebAssembly versions available for use in a browser). And while commenters
on Hacker News
and
elsewhere
have
taken pains
to point out the new software’s many current shortcomings, Thomas make the grandiose promise that
the current “super early alpha” state
will soon lead to something just as functional as anything Adobe has ever put out.
“We’re going to reach 100% [feature] parity within a month,” Thomas
stated on Reddit
of his plans to quickly squash bugs and add features with the help of community reports. Days later,
on Hacker News
, he amended that position slightly to say that “99% parity will take a while, but I’m sure it’ll be measured in months and not years.”
Is software over?
Thomas, who says he has about a decade of experience working on large-scale Rust projects,
wrote on Hacker News
that he was inspired to create his own open source Adobe software alternatives after being “bit by the dark pattern ‘cancellation fee’ one too many times.” Development of the totally free options offered here under MIT/Apache licenses will be funded, Thomas
wrote
, by selling token-based access to
the pre-existing Artcraft visual AI model and IDE
, which is offered as an imagery-generation option inside the apps alongside third-party models. This revenue stream will help ensure these apps aren’t “going to be some orphaned small-team project,” Thomas wrote. “We have a team building popular software for filmmakers, so supporting this is fully funded.”
Thomas is the
latest in a long line
of coders using AI tools to speed up the
long-standing but labor-intensive practice
of reverse engineering (i.e., replicating the functionality of a piece of software without directly copying the code itself). While that practice has
generally been found legally acceptable
, the ArtCraft apps
could still face legal trouble
if their “trade dress” too closely mimics Adobe’s familiar appearance and interface.
After coding exclusively with AI tools since February, Thomas
said
he foresees a near future when everyday developers can re-create open source versions of popular paid software to “take back the internet and own tech forever.”
“Now you can just create 1:1 functional equivalents, clean room, that are highly performant and cross-platform. Nothing is stopping you,” Thomas wrote. “We’ll replace Google Search, we’ll build our own smartphones, we’ll build better infra. We’ll remove all the ads and de-enshittify the entire tech world.”
“Software is over,” he gloated in
an earlier comment
, claiming to have “one-shotted Photoshop. The whole thing.”
